# Direct Action

## By the end of today

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
You will be able to treat the First Amendment as a toolkit and place common tactics on a spectrum from petition to civil disobedience.
:::

## Where this fits

Voting is the most familiar civic act.

It is not the most powerful one.

## The First Amendment package

- Speech — the message
- Press — the amplifier
- Assembly — the group
- Petition — the ask

Texas Article I, §§ 8 and 27 cover the same ground.

## Organized contact

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Coordinated calls, mail, and meetings. Petition with a list.
:::

Low legal risk. High effort. Austin is a bus ride away.

## Protest and marches

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Assembly plus speech in public space.
:::

## Citizen journalism

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Document and publish what officials do. That is press.
:::

## Filming the police

A clearly established First Amendment right in public, if you do not interfere.

*Turner v. Driver* (5th Cir. 2017): a "basic, vital, and well-established liberty."

## Civil disobedience

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Public, nonviolent, intentional lawbreaking. Arrest is part of the point.
:::

This is where First Amendment protection ends.

## Two directions of watching

**Panopticon:** the few watch the many.

**Reverse:** the many watch the few.

## Flock and mass ALPRs

Persistent cameras that store ordinary movement.

Citizen pushback is Direct Action against a general search in slow motion.

## Texas campus test

SB 2972 tried to ban campus "expressive activities" from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m.

A federal judge blocked that piece: "The First Amendment does not have a bedtime."

## Recap

- One toolkit, not four slogans
- Tactics sit on a risk spectrum
- Watching runs both directions
- The live tests are local

## Top Hat

- T/F: Filming on-duty police from a public sidewalk is unprotected in the 5th Circuit.
- MC: Civil disobedience is best described as:
- Likert: "More cameras on police improve conduct more than they relocate misconduct."
- Likert: "A city should need particularized suspicion before querying a stored plate database."
